Bidding resolves the next lot; you may also post an indicative price, announce a bidding ceiling, or sponsor Bidder 1. Scoring: Lots are worth 4, 6 and 10. Rivals: A live player controls each other seat, choosing its actions from its own observations and the game history.

All lots are sold, so bidding is dead. Sponsoring Bidder 1 would actually backfire: each sponsorship costs me 1 coin and adds 1 to their score, so my best finish is 20 (15 + finder's fee) versus Bidder 1's 18 — but only if I stay out of it. Their 4-point lead over Bidder 2 looks safe since Bidder 2 has no path to reputation. I'll use this turn on a free clerk quote to confirm no further lots exist before committing to idle talk for the remaining rounds.
